pages.title: Salt pan
pages.text: The pan has two states: $(thing)stage=0$() dry, $(thing)stage=1$() wet.$(br2)When water is directly above it — or flows in and triggers a neighbour update — it turns wet and schedules a $(bold)200-tick (10 s)$() delay. When the delay ends it clears the water above; if that space is now air, the pan returns to dry and a separate Salt Pile block appears above it.

pages.title: Salt pile
pages.text: The pile is its own block with $(thing)stage$() 0~2. It grows on $(bold)random ticks$(): the block above must be air, and each random tick has a 1/3 chance to advance one stage.$(br2)Breaking it drops 1 / 2 / 3 salt depending on stage, with Fortune. Breaking the pile $(bold)never$() breaks the pan below. Only when the pan itself is removed does the pile drop, so nothing is left floating.

pages.title: River silt
pages.text: River silt is a block entity acting as a farming bed: right-click with a farmable aquatic product to plant. The seed, result and total time all come from a $(thing)river_silt_farming$() recipe.$(br2)Growth advances by $(bold)+1 per tick$(); it is mature once growth reaches the recipe's $(thing)time$() and cannot be harvested before that.

pages.title: Fertilising and placement
pages.text: Using aquatic feed on silt speeds it up: growth is pushed forward, and reaching the total time matures it.$(br2)Planted items get a small horizontal offset and a random heading, so a bed never looks like a straight line — this is purely visual and does not affect any check.
